MINUTES
  INGLEWOOD SPECIAL PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  TUESDAY, AUGUST 24, 2021

(1) PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE:

The City of Inglewood Planning Commission held its Special Planning
Commission meeting on Tuesday, August 24, 2021 in the Council
Chambers on the ninth floor, in City Hall. Following the Pledge of
Allegiance by Commissioner Rice, the meeting was called to order
at 7:01 p.m.

(2) ROLL CALL:

Present:  Commissioner Patricia Patrick
  Commissioner David Rice
  Commissioner Aide’ Trejo
  Commissioner Cheryl Shaw Williams
  Chairman Larry Springs

Staff:  Mindy Wilcox, AICP, Planning Manager
  Eddy Ikemefuna, Senior Planner
  Bernard McCrumby, Senior Planner (Library Lecture Hall)
  Arturo Salazar, Planner (Library Lecture Hall)
  Marissa Fewell, Planner
  Christopher E. Jackson, Sr., Director of E.C.D.
  Cynthia Robinson, Secretary
  Jeff Lewis, Assistant City Attorney

(3) STAFF COMMUNICATIONS:

Ms. Wilcox stated that staff is available in the Library Lecture
Hall if Spanish translation is needed.

(4) PUBLIC COMMENTS:

None.

(5) PUBLIC HEARING:

5A.  Transit  Oriented  Development  (TOD)  Plans  for
Westchester/Veterans and Crenshaw/Imperial Plan Areas. A public
hearing to consider the following items associated with the TOD
Plans:
   Environmental Impact Report EA-EIR-2021-066 (EA-EIR-
  2021-066) to assess the proposed TOD Plans effects to
  the environment and community; and

    General Plan Amendment No. 2021-001 (GPA-2021-001) to
  modify the Land Use and Circulation Elements of the
  Inglewood General Plan for the TOD Plans; and

    Zone Change No. 2021-001 (ZC-2021-001) to establish
  Zoning Designations contained within the TOD Plans; and

    Zoning Code Amendment No. 2021-004 (ZCA-2021-004) to
  Chapter 12 of the Inglewood Municipal Code to establish
  regulations for the TOD Plans; and

    Establish Design Guidelines for the TOD Plans.

Ms. Wilcox reminded everyone to speak close to the microphone.
 Inglewood Special Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
August 24, 2021

Ms. Wilcox stated that Staff has requested that Public Comments be
taken tonight and the item be continued to October 6, 2021 to allow
staff time to respond to general questions that have come up from
the public through phone calls and emails. Additionally, Ms. Wilcox
noted that staff will be preparing a frequently asked questions
handout that will be posted on the Transit Oriented Development
Page of the Planning Division website that will be posted on the
website in the next two weeks.

Chairman Springs opened up the floor for public comments in regards
to the item.

Mr. Bernard McCrumby stated that the individuals in the Library
Lecture Hall could not hear Chairman Springs when he opened up the
floor for comments and that there is a group of people that would
like to speak.

The Secretary was asked and did re-read the item 5A.

Ms. Wilcox re-stated that Staff has requested that Public Comments
be taken tonight and the item be continued to October 6, 2021 to
allow staff time to respond to general questions that have come up
from the public through phone calls and emails. Additionally, Ms.
Wilcox noted that staff will be preparing a frequently asked
questions handout that will be posted on the Transit Oriented
Development Page of the Planning Divisions website that will be
posted on the website in the next two weeks.

Chairman Springs opened up the floor for public comments in regards
to item 5A.

PUBLIC COMMENTS:

 1. Alice Joyce – Inglewood Resident stated that the letter was
  Unclear.
 2. Melissa Barlow – Inglewood Resident stated that the letter was
  unclear and she was against the increase in density to
  the neighborhood. She stated she wants the residents to be
  better educated about the proposal.
 3. Brenda Tate Spears – Inglewood Resident stated that the letter
  is unclear and she would like a thorough explanation of what
  the TOD is and how it is going to impact the residents of the
  city.
 4. Teresa Kyles – Inglewood Resident is concerned about the
  clarity of the letter and that the TOD is not a priority.
 5. Christina Renae – Inglewood home owner is concerned about the
  density increase, the rezoning and the noise of construction.
 6. Arthur Jupiter – Hawthorne Resident that is concerned that the
  project will run under his home.
 7. S. Hummit – Inglewood Resident asked for more transparency on
  how it will impact the residents. She stated that she is
  concerned that homes will be lost.
 8. Debra Bruggman – Inglewood Resident is concerned about rezoning
  and asked for more transparency.
 9. Edwina Owens Sims – Inglewood Resident stated that she was
  concerned about being displaced.
10. Benjamin Gomez – Inglewood Resident and owner of three
  properties state that he is concerned about his property being
  taken away.
11. Melissa Hebert – Inglewood Resident stated that the letter did
  not have clear information.
12. Leroy Fischer – Inglewood Resident is against the TOD plan.

  2
 Inglewood Special Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
August 24, 2021
13. Lydia Castro – Father is an Inglewood Resident and Refuse
  Worker who is considering not to retire due to the a poorly
  Written letter he received. She stated that her parents are
  Very stressed because they feel they will be displaced.

Chairman Springs asked if there was a motion on the floor to
continue the public hearing.

MOTION:

The motion was made by Commissioner Patrick to continue the
discussion for item 5A to October 6, 2021 at 7:00pm for the reasons
noted earlier by the Planning Manager, Mindy Wilcox and the motion
was second by Commissioner Trejo.

Chairman Springs had asked if during or prior to the next public
hearing if someone will go over Item 5a to explain exactly what is
happening with the TOD.

Ms. Wilcox said yes at the October 6 meeting we will have a staff
member give a thorough presentation. She stated that staff has
heard the concerns expressed today loud and clear and we will do
our best to ensure that those concerns and questions are addressed
in the presentation as well as the frequently asked questions hand
out that Staff will be preparing in the next two weeks.

Chairman Springs asked if the information on the TOD is online.
Ms. Wilcox stated yes and that there is a link on the Public Notice
to the Plan itself which is on the City’s website.

The motion passed by the following roll call vote:

Ayes: Commissioners  Patrick,  Rice,  Trejo,  Shaw-Williams  and
Chairman Springs.

Chairman Springs stated that the vote was to continue the Public
Hearing so we will be able to address the public’s questions and
there will be an explanation on the TOD at the October 6, 2016
meeting. He asked if there were any other questions from the
general public. Seeing none, he closed the public speaking segment
and called for Commission Initiatives.

(9) COMMISSION INITIATIVES:

Chairman Springs asked if there will be stricter parking
enforcement and signage in the surrounding area with regards to
Sofi Stadium events.
Ms. Wilcox stated that Staff can coordinate with Public Works to
get that information to him. Chairman Springs asked if parking
regulations were not going to be enforced until September 1. Mindy
stated that she will confirm that information.

Chairman Springs stated that September 14th is a voting date and
it is very important that you vote.
